root_cause.text: The ALSA ctxfi virtual memory code incorrectly assumed multiple device page table pages were supported after CT_PTP_NUM was raised, but ct_vm_map() still maps only through vm->ptp[0].area, so allocations beyond a single PTP’s PTE capacity overrun that page table.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states “ct_vm_map() always uses PTEs in vm->ptp[0].area regardless of CT_PTP_NUM” and explains that after commit 391e69143d0a increased CT_PTP_NUM from 1 to 4, aggregate allocations exceeding one PTP’s 512-PTE/2M coverage caused ct_vm_map() to access beyond allocated space and fault; the fix simply reverts `#define CT_PTP_NUM 4` back to `1`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Reduce the configured number of device page table pages from four to one, changing device page table sizing and capacity.
intent_record.what: The macro definition of CT_PTP_NUM in ctvmem.h was changed from 4 to 1, reducing the configured number of device page table pages.
intent_record.how: At runtime, any code that uses CT_PTP_NUM will now allocate, size, or manage only one device page table page instead of four, decreasing the page table capacity and changing related memory usage and address mapping limits.

grouping_result.intent: Reduce the configured number of device page table pages from four to one, changing device page table sizing and capacity.

relevance_review.reason: The vulnerability stems from code only using a single device page table page while configuration allowed multiple pages. Reducing the configured page table count from four to one directly aligns the configuration with the actual single-page mapping behavior, preventing the overrun condition.

vuln_statements.stmt_text: #define CT_PTP_NUM	4	/* num of device page table pages */
vuln_statements.explanation: This statement increased the configured number of device page table pages to four, causing the virtual memory code to assume capacity beyond a single page table page. Because mapping logic still used only vm->ptp[0].area, this created the mismatch that allowed allocations to overrun the actual mapped page table.
